traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.5, 0.5, 0.48], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's subalpine fir review (Uchytil 1991, read 2026-10-16): "The typical form often grows to heights of 60 to 100 feet (18-30 m)"; "Trees up to 130 feet (40 m) tall ... have been found but are rare".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's subalpine fir review (Uchytil 1991, read 2026-10-16): "Needles are blunt tipped, flattened, and 1 to 1.2 inches (2.5-3 cm) long".

traits.crown_form.note: FEIS (Uchytil 1991), Abies lasiocarpa: "an extremely narrow and dense crown with short branches"; the photographed mature and old open-grown trees (inaturalist-crowns-2026-10) are .3 to .5 of their height across with near-parallel sides, a column more than the cone a young one is.

traits.foliage_ranks.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 66, Abies lasiocarpa: leaves "crowded, becoming erect by the curving of the lower", not two-ranked.

traits.cone_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 66, Abies lasiocarpa: "cones oblong- cylindric, 6-10 cm. long, dark purple".

generator.params.apical.note: Old conifers (pinidae revision 13): fitted with the family's ramifying crown (side_order 2, twig_years 10) so the drawn crown's widths at each tenth of height match the photographed open-grown trees': young (4 trees) .47 .53 .51 .47 .36 .26 .19 .18 .12 .05; mature (3) .36 .42 .43 .42 .37 .30 .21 .16 .10 .04; drawn 60 years .31 .36 .40 .36 .34 .31 .23 .15 .07 .04; 150 years .27 .35 .40 .38 .36 .33 .29 .24 .14 .03. apical sets the young crown's width.

generator.params.branch_reach.note: Old conifers (pinidae revision 13): fitted with the family's ramifying crown (side_order 2, twig_years 10) so the drawn crown's widths at each tenth of height match the photographed open-grown trees': young (4 trees) .47 .53 .51 .47 .36 .26 .19 .18 .12 .05; mature (3) .36 .42 .43 .42 .37 .30 .21 .16 .10 .04; drawn 60 years .31 .36 .40 .36 .34 .31 .23 .15 .07 .04; 150 years .27 .35 .40 .38 .36 .33 .29 .24 .14 .03. branch_reach, the wood at which a limb's yearly shoot is halved, sets how far old limbs spread.

generator.params.bole.note: Old conifers (pinidae revision 13): the share of an old tree's height cleared of limbs, cleared in step with height so saplings keep limbs to the ground: photographed trees keep limbs to the ground at every stage (crown base .01 to .05); the spire stays narrow, so its limbs stop lengthening early (branch_reach 3).

generator.params.note: Grand fir's values, changed by hand for subalpine fir: a shorter tree (height_rate set as for whitebark pine), an extremely narrow spire of short branches, the lower ones drooping (FEIS, Uchytil 1991: "an extremely narrow and dense crown with short branches"). Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 12 m and 25 cm across at 60 years in a stand; FEIS: "Subalpine fir grows very slowly" (Uchytil 1991). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: thin, grey, smooth young bark (FEIS: "Bark on young trees is thin, gray, and smooth"); bluish green needles (Abrams 1923 p. 66); dark purple cones.
